the-field-of-the-cloth-of-gold

In 1520 King Henry VIII of England and King Francis I of France met near Calais in a huge display of tents, banquets and tournaments, each trying to look richer than the other. This painting of about 1545 shows the festival soon after Henry and the pope split apart, when the age of Catholic Europe was ending.
the-council-of-trent

Bishops fill a great hall at the Council of Trent, held between 1545 and 1563 to answer the Protestant Reformation and reform the Catholic Church. Pasquale Cati painted this view of the council in 1588.
henry-viii-s-first-interview-with-anne-boleyn
King Henry VIII meets Anne Boleyn in a palace hall, the beginning of the romance that led him to break with the Catholic Church. Daniel Maclise painted this imagined meeting in 1836.
the-great-matter

Catherine of Aragon kneels before her husband Henry VIII at a church court in 1529, begging him not to end their marriage. Henry's 'Great Matter' was getting this annulled, which led England to leave the Catholic Church. Emanuel Leutze painted it in 1846.
portrait-of-pope-paul-iii
Pope Paul III, the pope who called the Council of Trent and approved the new Jesuit order, in a portrait painted by Titian in 1543. He led the Catholic response to the Reformation.
the-armada-portrait-of-elizabeth-i

Queen Elizabeth I rests her hand on a globe, a symbol that she ruled the seas, while behind her are scenes of the Spanish Armada's defeat in 1588. This is the most famous portrait of an English queen and was painted to celebrate the victory.
the-defeat-of-the-spanish-armada

English fireships drift into the Spanish fleet at night in 1588 and the great Armada scatters in a blaze of flames. Philip James de Loutherbourg painted it in 1796, long after the event, to show off British sea power.
english-ships-and-the-spanish-armada-august-1588
A crowd of English and Spanish ships sail in the crescent formation of the Spanish Armada in this painting made not long after the battle of 1588. It is one of the earliest pictures of the event.
the-rainbow-portrait-of-elizabeth-i

Elizabeth I, about 70 years old, holds a rainbow and wears a cloak covered in eyes and ears, a symbol of how much she saw. The painting from around 1602 shows her as ageless and wise, as she wished to be remembered.
elizabeth-i
Elizabeth I in a huge white ruff and jeweled gown, painted around 1595 by Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger. Portraits of Elizabeth were made carefully to make the queen look powerful and never old.
the-procession-portrait-of-elizabeth-i
Elizabeth I is carried in a grand procession by her courtiers and noblemen, like the center of a parade. This portrait from about 1601 shows how splendid her court was in her last years.
philip-ii-of-spain
Philip II, King of Spain, as a young prince in glittering armor and white hose. Titian painted him in 1551, and Philip later married Queen Mary I of England and sent the Armada against Elizabeth.
mary-i-of-england

Mary I, queen of England from 1553 to 1558, tried to bring England back to the Catholic Church and was nicknamed 'Bloody Mary' by her enemies. Antonis Mor painted her in 1554, the year she married Philip of Spain.
mary-queen-of-scots
Mary, Queen of Scots, was Elizabeth I's cousin and rival, held prisoner in England for 19 years before she was beheaded in 1587. This small portrait shows her in the 1560s.
sir-francis-walsingham

Sir Francis Walsingham, Elizabeth I's spymaster, uncovered plots against the queen, including the one that led to the downfall of Mary, Queen of Scots. John de Critz painted this portrait of him in 1589, near the time of the Armada.
the-death-of-queen-elizabeth-i
The old queen sits on cushions on the floor of her room, refusing to go to bed, while her courtiers watch anxiously. Paul Delaroche painted this sad scene of Elizabeth I's last days in 1828.
mary-queen-of-scots-the-farewell-to-france
Eighteen-year-old Mary, Queen of Scots, stands on a ship leaving the shores of France in 1561, where she grew up, to return to Scotland. Robert Herdman painted this farewell in 1867.
the-surrender-of-breda

The Dutch governor hands the keys of the city of Breda to the Spanish general Spinola in 1625, and Spinola kindly stops him from kneeling. Diego Velázquez painted it around 1635 and the forest of spears gave it the nickname Las Lanzas.
the-ratification-of-the-treaty-of-munster

Delegates from Spain and the Dutch Republic raise their hands to swear to the peace treaty of 1648 that ended the Eighty Years' War. Gerard ter Borch, who was there, painted it as a group of tiny, lifelike portraits.
the-battle-of-white-mountain

In 1620 the Catholic army defeated the Protestant Bohemian forces outside Prague on the White Mountain, an early victory in the Thirty Years' War. Peter Snayers painted the whole sweeping battlefield.
the-defenestration-of-prague

In 1618 angry Protestant nobles threw two Catholic officials out of a window of Prague Castle. They survived by landing in a pile of rubbish, but it started the Thirty Years' War. The Czech painter Václav Brožík painted the dramatic scene in 1890.
the-battle-of-lutzen-1632
Armies clash across a wide plain at the Battle of Lützen in 1632, where the Swedish king Gustavus Adolphus won the battle but was killed. Peter Snayers painted it in 1642.
the-sack-of-magdeburg-1631

An army attacks the German city of Magdeburg in 1631, one of the worst moments of the Thirty Years' War, when most of the city was destroyed. This engraving was made in the workshop of Matthäus Merian.
banquet-of-the-amsterdam-civic-guard-in-celebration-of-

Members of Amsterdam's civic guard celebrate the Peace of Münster in 1648 at an enormous feast, a group portrait of dozens of men in their Sunday best. Bartholomeus van der Helst painted it in the year peace came.
allegory-of-the-peace-of-westphalia
Jacob Jordaens fills a canvas with gods, figures and symbols of peace to celebrate the Peace of Westphalia, the treaties of 1648 that ended the Thirty Years' War. He painted it in 1654.
iconoclasts-in-a-church

Rioters climb ladders to smash saints' statues and stained glass inside a church, as Protestants did during the Dutch Revolt of the 1500s. Dirck van Delen painted this scene of church-breaking in 1630.
dutch-ships-ramming-spanish-galleys-off-the-flemish-coa

A tall Dutch warship rams Spanish galleys off the coast of Flanders in a battle of the long Dutch fight for independence from Spain. Hendrick Cornelisz. Vroom, the first great Dutch painter of ships, painted it in 1617.
before-the-battle-of-the-downs

Dutch and Spanish fleets face each other before the Battle of the Downs in 1639, where the Dutch admiral Tromp destroyed a Spanish fleet off the English coast. Reinier Nooms painted it around that year.
prince-maurice-at-the-battle-of-nieuwpoort-1600
Prince Maurice of Orange leads on a white horse at the Battle of Nieuwpoort in 1600, a big Dutch victory over the Spanish in the fight for independence. The painting was made later, in the 1800s.
the-siege-defense-of-a-church-courtyard-during-the-thir
Defenders hold out in a churchyard during the Thirty Years' War, with a stormy sky overhead. Carl Friedrich Lessing painted this dramatic scene in 1848.
the-maidens-of-magdeburg
In the legend of the siege of Magdeburg in 1631, young women of the city are in desperate danger as the city falls. Eduard Steinbrück painted this sad scene of the Thirty Years' War in 1866.
the-first-thanksgiving-at-plymouth
The Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people share a harvest meal in the autumn of 1621, the event we remember as the first Thanksgiving. Jennie Augusta Brownscombe painted this friendly gathering in 1914.
embarkation-of-the-pilgrims
The Pilgrims pray on the deck of the Speedwell in the Dutch port of Delfshaven in 1620 before sailing to America. Robert Walter Weir painted this in 1843 for the US Capitol.
the-landing-of-the-pilgrims
The Pilgrims row ashore at Plymouth in December 1620, in a famous painting by Henry Bacon of 1877. The idea of the Pilgrims stepping onto Plymouth Rock is a later tradition.
pilgrims-going-to-church
Pilgrims walk through the snow to church, with muskets over their shoulders in case of danger. George Henry Boughton painted the scene in 1867 as an image of the settlers' faith and courage.
mayflower-in-plymouth-harbor
The Mayflower, the ship that carried about 100 Pilgrims to America in 1620, rests in the harbor at sunset while a boat heads to shore. William Halsall painted it in 1882.
the-mayflower-compact-1620

The men of the Mayflower sign an agreement to make fair laws and govern themselves in the new colony. The Mayflower Compact of 1620 is one of the earliest steps toward self-government in America. Jean Leon Gerome Ferris painted it in 1899.
thanksgiving-at-plymouth

Pilgrims and Wampanoag people gather for the harvest feast of 1621, which later became Thanksgiving. Jennie Augusta Brownscombe painted this version in 1925 after she had painted the subject many times.
the-marriage-of-pocahontas
Pocahontas, the daughter of the Powhatan chief, marries the English settler John Rolfe in 1614, a wedding that brought a few years of peace to Virginia. Henry Brueckner painted it in 1855.
pocahontas

A portrait of Pocahontas, the young Powhatan woman who became known to the English settlers at Jamestown and later traveled to England, where she died in 1617. This engraving was made in 1858 from an older portrait.
the-landing-of-roger-williams-in-1636

After being banished from the Massachusetts colony for his beliefs, Roger Williams is welcomed by Narragansett people in 1636 and founds Providence, Rhode Island, as a place of religious freedom. Alonzo Chappel painted it in 1857.
party-for-new-year-s-day-in-new-amsterdam-1636
Dutch settlers in the colony of New Amsterdam on Manhattan, the future New York, celebrate New Year's Day in the snow. George Henry Boughton painted this cozy imagined scene in 1870.
courtship-in-new-amsterdam
A young Dutch couple meets in the days when New York was still the Dutch town of New Amsterdam. Francis William Edmonds painted this gentle scene of colonial life in 1850.
view-of-new-amsterdam
This watercolor shows the small Dutch town of New Amsterdam on the tip of Manhattan, with windmills, ships and a fort. It was drawn in 1664, the year the English took it over and renamed it New York.
pocahontas-at-the-court-of-king-james
Pocahontas, dressed as an English lady, is presented to King James I in London in 1616. Richard Rummell made this colorful picture in 1907, three hundred years after the founding of Jamestown.
the-eve-of-the-battle-of-edge-hill-1642
Cavaliers and soldiers share a quiet meal and some rest before the first big battle of the English Civil War in 1642. Charles Landseer painted this calm before the storm in 1845.
cromwell-at-the-battle-of-naseby-1645
Oliver Cromwell leads the cavalry charge at Naseby in 1645, the battle where Parliament's New Model Army won the English Civil War. Charles Landseer painted it in 1851.
